div.p: Avionics full duplex switched Ethernet network (AFDX), based on IEEE802.3, has been developed as a costeffective avionic network to replace the low-speed ARINC 429 which has limited bandwidth and limited addressing capability. For avionic real-time electronic system, delay and delay jitter are the most important parameters that must be guaranteed for some data such as the data for piloting plane. But the competition of the resource of the scheduler between multiple Virtual Links will result in delay and jitter in the AFDX network and the jitter would become unacceptable when the data flow passes through multiple-hops. In this paper, we introduce a jitter-EDD mechanism into the AFDX network. It can regulate the data flows on the AFDX network components and significantly reduce the end-to-end jitter. In order to assure that every frame can be sent to the physical link before its deadline, we also do schedulability analysis for the schedulers.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Due to the increasing amount of communication requirements, Avionics Full Duplex Switch Ethernet (AFDX) which is based Ethernet 802.3 has been developed as the next generation aircraft data bus. Comparing to the low-speed ARINC 429, the AFDX extremely increase the bandwidth up to 100Mbps.

The AFDX uses a Full Duplex Link to eliminate the collisions on the point-to-point links level that caused by the access method CSMA/CD [1]. The 100Mbps Link can be distributed into multiple Virtual Links, and a 16-bit value called a Virtual Link ID is used to route Ethernet frames in an AFDX network. In order to prevent the traffic on one virtual link from the interfering with traffic on other virtual links using the same physical links, the AFDX limiting the rate at which Ethernet frames can be transmitted on a virtual link and the size of the Ethernet frames. Each virtual link is assigned two parameters which help guarantee the QoS required for avionics systems: BAG( it represents the minimum interval in milliseconds between Ethernet frames that are transmitted on the virtual link) and Lmax( the largest Ethernet frame that can be transmitted on the virtual link).To increase the reliability of the system, an AFDX network consists of two redundant networks-network A and network B, in default mode each frame is transmitted on parallel over the two redundant networks [2].

The problem is that multiple Virtual Links that will pass through the same physical link will complete the resource of scheduler which is responsible for choosing a frame between all the Virtual Links and putting it on to the physical line and this will result in delay and jitter. The end-to-end delay and jitter would become unacceptable when the data flow passes through multiple-hops network.

There already exists some research for the end-to-end delay analysis. Hussein Charara built a simulation model with QNAP2 to analysis the end-to-end delay and study the performance of the AFDX [3]. Mifdaoui et al. used network calculus to give transmission delay analysis for 1553B bus [4]. Fraboul et al. used the stochastic network calculus theory and trajectory approach to compute end-toend delay bound in AFDX network [5]. The characteristics of real-time communication applications are very unlike those that are non-realtime. [9] showed some general introduction about real-time communication network. The article [8] [6] did some research about the schedulability analysis of real-time scheduling. The methods for delay jitter control on the network has been discussion in [10].

In this paper, we introduce a jitter-EDD mechanism into the AFDX network. It can regulate the data flows on the AFDX network components and significantly reduce the end-to-end jitter. In order to assure that every frame can be sent to the physical link before its deadline, we also do schedulability analysis for the schedulers. At last, we use SimEvents to build a model for the simulation.

The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 presents the jitter-EDD mechanism and section 3 presents our model. In section 4, we will do analysis for the model and then the simulation in section 5. Section 6 is the conclusion.

div.head: II. THE JITTER-EDD MECHANISM
div.p: The jitter-EDD(Earliest-Due-Date)'s algorithm [10] extends delay-EDD to provide a bound on the end-to-end delay jitter which is originally designed for packet switching networks. Consider an EDF scheduler and assume that every packet sent on the outgoing link carries a field with the difference between its deadline and the actual finishing time. A jitter-EDD regulator at the entrance of the next server holds the packet until its eligibility time. The jitter-EDD regulator, one for each of the channel, sufficiently faithfully preserves the original arrival pattern of the packets. Figure 1 shows the progress of a packet through two adjacent servers.

In the first server, the packet is served seconds before its deadline. So, it is made eligible to be scheduled after seconds in the next server. Since there is a constant delay between the eligibility times of the packet at two adjacent servers, the packet stream can be provided a delay jitter bound. An end-to-end path can be considered as a concatenation of independent node pairs, so the end-to-end delay jitter can be bounded. In the originally jitter-EDD scheme, there is no jitter-EDD regulator at the destination host, the end-to-end delay jitter bound is the same as the local delay bound at the last server. But in order to increase the safety of the avionics applications data, we modify the originally jitter-EDD scheme. We also put a jitter-EDD regulator at the destination host. The jitter-EDD algorithm may increase the average delay of the packets and decrease the average throughput of the server. But in general, it providesbetter jitter control. In our scheme, the end-to-end jitter on the AFDX networks can be reduced to zero. The sending End System is the device that send the data that comes from the application software and going into the buffer onto the AFDX physical link, as shown in Figure 2. In our model, the scheduler is a EDF(earliest deadline first) scheduler, it multiplexes the data that coming from different Virtual Link into one physical link. In order to guarantee the QOS of the network, the AFDX puts a regulator before the scheduler which keep that the minimum time interval between the first bits oftwo consecutive frames from the same virtual is BAG. The regulator is a special buffer that it fetches a frame from the buffer before it in a constant interval time -BAG and then the frame can be scheduled by the scheduler. When a frame can be scheduled , we name the time .When the frame have been scheduled by the scheduler, and will be going out of the sending End System, we name the time . From the configure table of the End System, we will know the deadline of the frame on the virtual link of the end system. We name the interval time , and it will be stamped into the frame header just before the frame will be going out of the end system. The frame will be sent paralleling on the redundancy two physical link-network A and network B. Our switch is an output buffer switch, as shown in Figure 3. The input buffer size is one. When the frame is sent to the switch, the routing module will send it to the corresponding jitter-EDD regulator according to the Virtual Link ID. We define the time that a frame arrives at the switch , the deadline of the frame on the switch d and the time when the frame has been scheduled by the scheduler and will be going out of the switch . The jitter-EDD regualtor is a special buffer that admits the scheduler picks the frame at an eligibility time which means that the scheduler can picks the frame only at the interval time . It is responsible for reconstructing and preserving the arrival pattern of frames along that virtual Link. Because of the speed of the routing module is much more quick than the output physical link, the time spent on the routing module can be ignored compared to the time spent in the output queues (here is the jitter-EDD regulator).The time interval that between the time when the frame can be scheduled by the last End system's or Switch's scheduler and the time when the frame can be scheduled by this system's is constant for every frame, and that time interval is d which is the deadline that has been distributed on the corresponding Virtual Link of last device if when we ignore the propagation delay between the two devices and the switching delay which is introduced by the routing module. It means that, in the points of the scheduler's view, the frames have been regulated by the jitter-EDD regulator and the time interval between two successive frames is BAG. We make the new , and stamp it into the frame. Because the maximum number of the virtual link on a physical link is 128, we have 128 jitter-EDD regualtors before every scheduler (the scheduler puts the data onto the physical link).

div.head: C. Receiving End System
div.p: As shown in Figure 4, when a frame arrive the receiving End System, it will be de-multiplexed into the corresponding jitter-EDD regulator by the virtual link ID according to the configure table of the end system. The jitter-EDD regulator here in the receiving End System have some difference with the jitter-EDD regulator in the switch .The jitter-EDD regulator will make the frame eligible at . Then it is the integrity check(IC) and Redundancy Management (RM). After this, the availably frame will be submitted to the application software. Here like the routing module in the switch, the time cost on the de-multiplex in the receiving End System will be ignored. The jitter-EDD regulator number is also 128.

div.head: B. deadline distribute
div.p: We have done detailed analysis for the end-to-end delay on the last part. Through those analysis, we can see that if we know the end-to-end delay limit D of Virtual Link i on the network, we distribute it into n parts, , , ..., , then we can guarantee the endto-end delay if all the task sets can be scheduled by the EDF scheduler.

As is known to all, the larger the load is, the larger the delay is. So, we give out a weight-allot method to allot the end-to-end delay D: (1) is the collection of Virtual Links that use the same scheduler with virtual link i in the network node k that virtual i pass through (Node 0 represents the sending End System, nodes 1…n-1 represent switches), is the largest frame length in the virtual link m, is the BAG of the Virtual Link m.

We may get different for the same Virtual Link on the redundancy network A and B, but the value must be only one because of the limit of the physical model. The solution is to take the larger one as and to distribute the remain delay on the remain network nodes.

div.head: C. Schedulability analysis
div.p: In order to guarantee the end-to-end delay and delay jitter, we must do schedulability analysis for every scheduler. The scheduling of the frame in the network is non-preemptive scheduling and [8] have done research about this analysis. According to Theorem 7 in [8], we can derivate our conclusion: Conclusion 1: A set of Virtual Links are schedulable if and only if both of the following hold: is the collection of Virtual Links that use the same scheduler with virtual link i in the network node k that virtual i pass through (Node 0 represents the sending End System, nodes 1…n-1 represent switches), is the largest frame lengthin the virtual link m, is the BAG of the Virtual Link m.

div.head: A. Simulation Scenario
div.p: We have built a platform with 9 switches, 13 End Systems, 9 virtual Links by SimEvents, as shown in the following figure: Virtual Links 1,4,5 send frames on both of redundancy network A and network B while the others send frames only on one network.We use the weight-allot method as described in 4.2 to distribute the end-to-end delay among the switches and End Systems.According to the schedulability analysis for all the schedulers in the network on above, we can get a conclusion that all the schedulers are schedulable.

div.head: B. Simulation Scenario
div.p: The jitter-EDD mechanism will reduce the end-to-end jitter, but it may increase the end-to-end delay. Figure 6 shows the difference between the system that uses jitter-EDD mechanism and the system that doesn't use jitter-EDD mechanism. As we can see, the delay of Virtual Link1 and Virtual Link4 with jitter-EDD mechanism is smaller than the delay of Virtual Link1 and Virtual Link4 without jitter-EDD mechanism while the end-to-end delay jitter of Virtual Link1 and Virtual Link4 with jitter-EDD is much smaller.
